task.description: Rework iteration 1 of Step 2 for ISS-0421: fix the single FAIL finding from step-02b (section 3b's max_concurrency: 2 for maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 was a hardcoded literal with no enforced or derived tie to Admission's independently-overridable reserved_headroom). Pick option (a) or (b) as named in the validator's routing instructions and specify it precisely; do not touch the 6 other sections/checks the validator already passed.

result.summary:
Chose option (a) -- a live accessor -- over option (b) (hardcoded literal + comment + equality test), and rejected (b) explicitly rather than defaulting to the api_pipeline.ex precedent uncritically. Reasoning stated in the design doc's revised §3b: reserved_headroom is GenServer state set at Admission.init/1 from whichever of (config default, config override, start_link/1 opts override) won -- it is not a plain module attribute or bare config read visible from outside the process. To write a test asserting 'Poller's literal == Admission's actual reserved_headroom', the test itself would need a way to read Admission's live value, i.e. it would need to build the same accessor this design adds anyway. Building that accessor for the test's sake only, and leaving the literal in the real Poller code path, would still carry the exact runtime drift hazard the validator flagged for any environment/deploy the test suite doesn't exercise (e.g. an Admission instance started with a start_link opts override outside test). Once the accessor exists, consuming it live at the real call site is strictly safer than building it only for a test and is no more implementation surface, so (a) subsumes (b)'s guarantee rather than adding a parallel, weaker one.

Specified precisely for ELIXIR-DEV: new Letflow.Admission.reserved_headroom/1 (default server \\ __MODULE__), mirroring the exact existing try_acquire/2 and release/2 idiom (admission.ex:184-190, 205-208) -- a GenServer.call/2 delegate plus one new handle_call(:reserved_headroom, _from, state) clause replying with the already-held state.reserved_headroom, no state mutation, purely additive (no existing Admission function's name/arity/spec/behavior changes). maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 calls this fresh every invocation (no caching, matching this design's own sweep_task_timeout_ms/0 and Letflow.Scheduler's established read-fresh convention) and uses the returned integer directly as that sweep's Task.async_stream max_concurrency. The safety arithmetic in §3b is now restated as an algebraic identity -- global_cap + max_concurrency = (pool_size - reserved_headroom) + reserved_headroom = pool_size -- that holds for ANY configured reserved_headroom value, not just the current default of 2, so it can no longer silently drift the way a hardcoded literal could.

Sections touched: §0 (affected-files line, now naming the additive Admission.ex accessor), §3b (full rewrite: decision + rejected-alternative reasoning + new accessor spec + restated arithmetic; open question at the end kept, reworded to note the revisit no longer needs a poller.ex edit), §3c (generalized 'max(8,2)' to 'max(global_cap, reserved_headroom)', current value kept as an example), §7 (added the new Admission accessor to the code-shape summary; updated the max_concurrency bullet and the 'no change to Admission' bullet, since Admission.ex is now touched additively), §8 (reworded the reserved_headroom-inventory open question to reflect that a future revisit only requires an Admission-side config change).

NOT touched: §1 (numbers/arithmetic baseline), §2 (sequential-sweep decision), §3a (the 8-for-six-sweeps bound), §4 (fault isolation: async_stream options, per-task rescue, AC1 net effect), §5 (AC4 preservation), §6 (REQ-219/ISS-0451 orthogonality) -- these are the parts step-02b already confirmed sound and the validator's routing instructions said not to touch. Confirmed via git diff that only the described lines in §0/§3b/§3c/§7/§8 changed.
result.routing: Route to Step 2b CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (re-check) to verify: (1) the new Letflow.Admission.reserved_headroom/1 accessor spec is unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without judgment and is genuinely additive (no change to try_acquire/2, release/2, or any existing handle_call clause); (2) the restated §3b arithmetic is correct and no longer depends on any hardcoded literal matching a separately-maintained config value; (3) no other section (§1, §2, §3a, §4, §5, §6) was altered from the version already passed in step-02b's 6 other findings.

next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for re-check of the reworked §3b/§7/§8 (and §0/§3c) sections only.

gate_history.notes: Admission.global_cap arithmetic (pool_size 10 - reserved_headroom 2 = 8) independently verified correct against admission.ex/api_pipeline.ex/config. Peak-concurrency safety argument in section 3b fails: max_concurrency:2 for maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 is a hardcoded literal that must stay equal to Admission's reserved_headroom for the 8+2=10 proof to hold, but nothing derives or enforces that equality -- a future independent change to reserved_headroom would silently break the pool-exhaustion safety bound. All other checks (fault isolation, AC4, sequential-sweep decision, no literal code, 2 of 3 open questions) passed.
